title: Islamic Computational Calendar
intro: This computational Islamic calendar represents Hijri lunar dates through ICU's astronomy-based algorithm rather than local crescent announcements.
structure: Twelve named lunar months generally have 29 or 30 days. Month boundaries are calculated rather than following a fixed alternating table.
model: The supported date range and astronomical calculation follow the ICU implementation. This is separate from the arithmetic Islamic Civil and tabular variants and the bounded Umm al-Qura table.
example: Ramadan is month nine; a local authority can announce its beginning on a different date from the calculated boundary.
history: Islamic date reckoning is rooted in the Hijri era. Communities use different calculation and crescent-observation methods for religious and civil events.
limits: Not a guarantee of historical or local crescent visibility, an official religious determination or a conversion beyond ICU's supported domain.
